questions.question: If \(\sin θ - \cos θ = \frac{1}{{29}}\) find the value of sinθ + cosθ.
questions.questionHtml: If \(\sin θ - \cos θ = \frac{1}{{29}}\) find the value of sinθ + cosθ.
questions.solution:
Given:

\(\sin θ - \cos θ = \frac{1}{{29}}\)

Formula used:

Sin2θ + Cos2θ = 1

Calculation:

Sinθ – Cosθ = 1/29

⇒ (Sinθ – Cosθ)2 = (1/29)2

⇒ Sin2θ + Cos2θ – 2SinθCosθ = 1/841

⇒ 1 – 2SinθCosθ = 1/841

⇒ 1 – 1/841 = 2SinθCosθ

⇒ 840/841 = 2SinθCosθ

(Sinθ + Cosθ)2

⇒ Sin2θ + Cos2θ + 2SinθCosθ

⇒ 1 + 840/841

⇒ {(841 + 840)/841}

⇒ 1681/841

⇒ 41/29

∴  The value of sinθ + cosθ is 41/29

Shortcut TrickIf (a)sinθ - (b)cosθ = c

then (a)cosθ + (b)sinθ = d

Then a2 + b2 = c2 + d2

So now from the equation;

⇒ 1 + 1 = 1/841 + d2

d2 = 2 - 1/841

d = 41/29

questions.question: If sin θ sec 2 θ = 2/3, 0° < θ < 90°, then the value of (tan 2 θ + sin 2 θ) is:
questions.questionHtml: If sin θ sec<sup>2</sup> θ = 2/3, 0° < θ < 90°, then the value of (tan<sup>2</sup> θ + sin<sup>2</sup> θ) is:
questions.solution:
Given:

sin θ sec2 θ = 2/3

Concept used:

Value putting method.

Calculation:

sinθ × sec2θ = 2/3 where θ° < θ < 90° 

Let us take θ = 30° 

sin30° = 1/2

sec30° = \(\frac{2}{{\sqrt 3 }}\)

sin30° × sec230° = \(\frac{1}{2} × {\left( {\frac{2}{{\sqrt 3 }}} \right)^2}\)

sin30° × sec230° = \(\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{4}{3} = \frac{2}{3}\)

Hence proved.

Now, (tan2θ + sin2θ) = (tan230° + sin230°)

(tan230° + sin230°) = \(\left( {{{\left( {\frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }}} \right)}^2} + {{\left( {\frac{1}{2}} \right)}^2}} \right)\)

(tan230° + sin230°) = \(\frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{4}\)

(tan230° + sin230°) = 7/12

questions.question: If 5 cos θ = 4 sin θ, 0° ≤ θ ≤ 90°, then what will be the value of sec θ?
questions.questionHtml: If 5 cos θ = 4 sin θ, 0° ≤ θ ≤ 90°, then what will be the value of sec θ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Given: 5 cos θ = 4 sin θ ⇒ tan θ = 5/4.

For a right-angled triangle, if Perpendicular = 5 and Base = 4, then Hypotenuse = √(52 + 42) = √41.

Since sec θ = Hypotenuse / Base, we get sec θ = √41 / 4.

∴ The correct answer is √41 / 4.

Alternate Method

Given: 5 cos θ = 4 sin θ and 0° ≤ θ ≤ 90°.

Formula Used: tan θ = sin θ / cos θ and sec2θ = 1 + tan2θ.

⇒ 5 cos θ = 4 sin θ

⇒ sin θ / cos θ = 5 / 4

⇒ tan θ = 5 / 4

⇒ sec2θ = 1 + (5 / 4)2

⇒ sec2θ = 1 + 25 / 16

⇒ sec2θ = (16 + 25) / 16 = 41 / 16

⇒ sec θ = √(41 / 16) = √41 / 4

∴ The correct answer is √41 / 4.

Additional Information

Trigonometric Identities

Fundamental relations: sin2θ + cos2θ = 1, 1 + tan2θ = sec2θ, and 1 + cot2θ = cosec2θ.

Right Triangle Ratios

sec θ is the reciprocal of cos θ. In a right triangle, sec θ = Hypotenuse / Base.

Pythagoras Theorem

In a right-angled triangle, Hypotenuse2 = Perpendicular2 + Base2.

questions.question: In right-angled triangle ABC, ∠B = 90º and angle A and angle C are acute angles. If cosecA = 2√2, then find the value of sinA . cosC + cosA . sinC.
questions.questionHtml: In right-angled triangle ABC, ∠B = 90º and angle A and angle C are acute angles. If cosecA = 2√2, then find the value of sinA . cosC + cosA . sinC.
questions.solution:
sinA = 1 / (2√2) ⇒ sin(A + C) = 1 ⇒ sinA . cosC + cosA . sinC = sinA . sinA + cosA . cosA ⇒ (1 / (2√2)) . (1 / (2√2)) + cosA . cosA

= (1 / 8) + (7 / 8) ⇒ 1

sec2 θ - tan2 θ = 1

Then,

2 secθ =  √3+ 1/√3

questions.question: If \(\tan a = \frac{2}{{\sqrt {13} }}\) , then the value of \(\frac{{cosec^2a\ +\ 2{{\sec }^2}a}}{{cosec^2a\ -\ 3{{\sec }^2}a}}\) is:
questions.questionHtml: If  \(\tan a = \frac{2}{{\sqrt {13} }}\), then the value of \(\frac{{cosec^2a\ +\ 2{{\sec }^2}a}}{{cosec^2a\ -\ 3{{\sec }^2}a}}\) is:
questions.solution:
Given:

tanα = 2/√13

Concept Used:

tanθ = Opposite side/Adjacent side

secθ = Hypotenuse/Adjacent side

cosecθ = Hypotenuse/Opposite side

  

Calculation:

Applying Pythagoras theorem;

⇒ H2 = 22 + (√13)2

⇒ H2 = 4 + 13

⇒ H = √17   

Cosecθ = √17/2 and Secθ = √17/√13

⇒ Cosec2θ = 17/4 and Sec2θ = 17/13

Putting values in the given equation,

⇒ {(17/4) + 2(17/13)}/{(17/4) – 3(17/13)} 

⇒ (17/4 + 34/13)/(17/4 – 51/13) 

⇒ {(221 + 136)/52}/{(221 – 204)/52}

⇒ 357/17

⇒ 21

∴ The value of \(\frac{{cosec^2a\ +\ 2{{\sec }^2}a}}{{cosec^2a\ -\ 3{{\sec }^2}a}}\)is 21.

questions.question: If \(\frac{cosec \theta+\cot \theta}{cosec \theta-\cot \theta}=7\) , then the value of \(\frac{4\sin^2\theta-1}{4\sin^2\theta+5}\) is:
questions.questionHtml: If \(\frac{cosec \theta+\cot \theta}{cosec \theta-\cot \theta}=7\), then the value of \(\frac{4\sin^2\theta-1}{4\sin^2\theta+5}\) is:
questions.solution:
Given:-

\(\frac{cosec θ+\cot θ}{cosec θ-\cot θ}=7\)

Concept used :-

Pythagoras's theorem and Trigonometric ratio.

Calculation:

According to question -

⇒ cosecθ + cotθ = 7cosecθ – 7cotθ 

⇒ 6cosecθ – 8cotθ = 0

⇒ 3cosecθ = 4cotθ 

⇒ 3 × 1/sinθ = 4 × cosθ/sinθ  

⇒ 3/sinθ = 4cosθ/sinθ 

⇒ cosθ = 3/4

By pythagoras theorem

P2 = h2 – b2

p2 = 42 – 32

p2 = 16 – 9

p2 = 7

⇒ p = √7

Now,

The value of \(\frac{4\sin^2\theta-1}{4\sin^2\theta+5}\) = (4 × 7/16 – 1)/(4 × 7/16 + 5)

⇒ (7/4 – 1)/(7/4 + 5)

⇒ (3/4)/(27/4)

⇒ 3/27

⇒ 1/9

∴ The value is 1/9

questions.question: if \(\sin θ=\frac{11}{15}\) then the value of (sec θ - tan θ) is:
questions.questionHtml: if \(\sin θ=\frac{11}{15}\) then the value of (sec θ - tan θ) is:
questions.solution:
Given:

sinθ = 11/15

Formula used:

b2 = √(h2 – p2)

sinθ = p/h

secθ = h/b

tanθ = p/b

Calculation:

We know that,

sinθ = p/h = 11/15

b2 = (h2 – p2)

⇒ b2 = ((15)2 – (11)2)

⇒ b2 = (225 – 121)

⇒ b2 = 104

⇒ b = 2√26

secθ = h/b = 15/2√26

tanθ = p/b = 11/2√26

 (sec θ –  tan θ) = (15/2√26 – 11/2√26)

⇒ 4/2√26

⇒ 2/√26

Multiplying numerator and denominator by √26 we get,

⇒ (2/√26 × √26/√26)

⇒ (2√26)/26

⇒ √26/13

∴ Required value is \(\frac{\sqrt{26}}{13}\)

questions.question: In ΔABC, if ∠B = 90°, AB = 21 cm and BC = 20 cm, then \(\rm \frac{1 \space +\space sinA \space -\space cosA}{1 \space + \space sinA \space + \space cosA}\) is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: In ΔABC, if ∠B = 90°, AB = 21 cm and BC = 20 cm, then \(\rm \frac{1 \space +\space sinA \space -\space cosA}{1 \space + \space sinA \space + \space cosA}\) is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given: 

AB = 21 cm, BC = 20 cm and angle B = 90º

Formula used:

By Pythagoras theorem

AC2 = AB2 + BC2

Calculation:

AC2 = 212 + 202 = 841

⇒ AC = 29 cm 

sin A = Perpendicular/Hyptotenuse =\(\frac{BC}{AC}\)

⇒ sin A = 20/29  

cos A = Base/ Hypotenuse = \(\frac{AB}{AC}\)

⇒ cos A = 21/29

\(\rm \frac{1 \space +\space sinA \space -\space cosA}{1 \space + \space sinA \space + \space cosA}\) = \(\rm \frac{1 \space +\space \frac{20}{29}\space -\space \frac{21}{29}}{1 \space + \space \frac{20}{29} \space + \space \frac{21}{29}}\)

⇒ \(\rm \frac{\space \space \frac{29 + 20 -21}{29}}{ \space \space \space \frac{29 + 20 +21}{29}}\)

⇒ \(\frac{28}{70}\) = \(\frac{2}{5}\)

∴ The required result = \(\frac{2}{5}\)

Mistake PointsPlease note that, in the question, we have sin A & cos A, it means in Δ ABC, we take θ for ∠A, and then BC & AB will be perpendicular & base respectively.

questions.question: If \(\frac{\sin ^{2} ∅-3 \sin ∅+2}{\cos ^{2} ∅}=1\) , where 0° < ∅ < 90°, then what is the value of (cos 2∅ - sin 3∅ + cosec 2∅)?
questions.questionHtml: If \(\frac{\sin ^{2} ∅-3 \sin ∅+2}{\cos ^{2} ∅}=1\), where 0° < ∅ < 90°, then what is the value of (cos 2∅ - sin 3∅ + cosec 2∅)?
questions.solution:
Given:

\(\frac{\sin ^{2} ∅-3 \sin ∅+2}{\cos ^{2} ∅}=1\)

Concept used:

Sin2θ + Cos2θ = 1

Calculation:

\(\frac{\sin ^{2} ∅-3 \sin ∅+2}{\cos ^{2} ∅}=1\)

⇒ sin2∅ - 3sin∅ + 2 = cos2∅

⇒ sin2∅ - 3sin∅ + 2 = 1 - sin2∅

⇒ 2sin2∅ - 3sin∅ + 1 = 0

⇒ 2sin2∅ - 2sin∅ - sin∅ + 1 = 0

⇒ 2sin∅(sin∅ - 1) - 1(sin∅ - 1) = 0

⇒ (sin∅ - 1)(2sin∅ - 1) = 0

⇒ sin∅ = 1 or 1/2

So, ∅ = 90° or 30°

∅ cannot be 90°  [As 0° < ∅ < 90°]

So, ∅ = 30°

Now,

(cos 2∅ - sin 3∅ + cosec 2∅) = (cos60° - sin90° + cosec60°)

⇒ (1/2) - 1 + (2/√3)

⇒ [(√3 - 2√3 + 4)/2√3]

⇒ [{(√3 - 2√3 + 4) × √3}/(2√3) × √3]

⇒ (3 - 6 + 4√3)/6

⇒ (- 3 + 4√3)/6

∴ Required answer is \(\frac{-3+4 \sqrt{3}}{6}\).

questions.question: If tan 4 x - tan 2 x = 1, then the value of sin 4 x + sin 2 x is:
questions.questionHtml: If tan<sup>4</sup> x - tan<sup>2</sup> x = 1, then the value of sin<sup>4</sup> x + sin<sup>2</sup> x is:
questions.solution:
Given:

tan4 x - tan2 x = 1

Formula used:

sec2x = 1 + tan2x

tanx = sinx/cosx

sin2x + cos2x = 1

Calcuation:

tan4 x - tan2 x = 1

⇒ tan4 x = 1 + tan2 x

⇒ tan4 x = sec2x

⇒ sin4x/cos4x = 1/cos2x

⇒ sin4x = cos2x

We have to find the value of sin4 x + sin2 x

⇒ sin4 x + sin2 x = cos2x + sin2x

∴ sin4 x + sin2 x  is 1

questions.question: If cosec θ = \(\frac{\sqrt 5}{2}\) , then what will be the value of (sec θ + tan θ - cot θ sin θ) ?
questions.questionHtml: If cosec θ = \(\frac{\sqrt 5}{2}\), then what will be the value of (sec θ + tan θ - cot θ sin θ) ?
questions.solution:
Given:

cosec θ = √5/2,

Hypotenuse = √5, Perpendicular = 2 and Base = 1

Now, sec θ + tan θ - cot θ sin θ

⇒ √5/1 + 2/1 - (1/2 × 2/√5)

⇒ 2 + 4√5/5

Alternate Method

Traditional method:

Given:

cosec θ = \(\frac{√ 5}{2}\)

Hence, sin θ = \(\frac{2}{√5}\)

Formula:

sin2 θ = 1 - cos2 θ

4/5 = 1 - cos2 θ

⇒ cos2 θ = 1 - 4/5 = 1/5

⇒ cos θ = \(\frac{1}{√5}\), sec θ = \(√5\) 

tan θ = sin θ / cos θ = \(\frac{2}{√5}\)/ \(\frac{1}{√5}\)

⇒ tan θ = 2 

Calculation:

(sec θ + tan θ - cot θ sin θ)

⇒ (sec θ + tan θ - cos θ/sin θ × sin θ)

⇒ (sec θ + tan θ - cos θ)

⇒ (\(√5\) + 2 - \(\frac{1}{√5}\)) 

⇒ 2 + 4/\(√5\))

⇒ 2 + 4\(√5\) × \(√5\)/\(√5\)

∴ The required answer = \(2 + \frac{4√ 5}{5}\)

questions.question: If secθ - tanθ = m, then 2 tanθ = ?

secθ - tanθ = m ........ 1

questions.question: If \(\frac{cosec^2 \theta}{cosec^2 \theta - \cot^2 \theta}=\frac{13}{4},0^{\circ}<\theta<90^{\circ}\) , then the value of \(\frac{52 \cos^2 \theta-9 \tan^2 \theta}{18 \sec^2 \theta + 8 \cot^2 \theta}\) will be:
questions.questionHtml: If \(\frac{cosec^2 \theta}{cosec^2 \theta - \cot^2 \theta}=\frac{13}{4},0^{\circ}<\theta<90^{\circ}\), then the value of \(\frac{52 \cos^2 \theta-9 \tan^2 \theta}{18 \sec^2 \theta + 8 \cot^2 \theta}\) will be:
questions.solution:
Given:

\(\frac{cosec^2 θ}{cosec^2 θ - \cot^2 θ}=\frac{13}{4},0^{\circ}<θ<90^{\circ}\)

Formula used:

cosec2θ = 1/sin2θ 

cot2θ = cos2θ/sin2θ 

1 – cos2θ = sin2θ 

B2 = H2 – P2

Calculation:

\(\frac{cosec^2 θ}{cosec^2 θ - \cot^2 θ}=\frac{13}{4},0^{\circ}<θ<90^{\circ}\)

⇒ 1/sin2θ/1/sin2θ – cos2θ/sin2θ = 13/4

⇒ 1/sin2θ/(1 – cos2θ)/sin2θ  = 13/4

⇒ 1/sin2θ/sin2θ/sin2θ = 13/4

⇒ 1/sin2θ = 13/4

⇒ sinθ = 2/√13 = P/H

Now,

B2 = H2 – P2

⇒ B2 = (√13)2 – (2)2

⇒ B2 = (13 – 4) = 9

⇒ B = 3

Now,

cosθ = B/H = 3/√13

tanθ = P/B = 2/3

secθ = H/B = √13/3

cotθ = B/P = 3/2

Now,

The value of \(\frac{52 \cos^2 \theta-9 \tan^2 \theta}{18 \sec^2 \theta + 8 \cot^2 \theta}\)

⇒ 52 × (3/√13)2 – 9 × (2/3)2/18 × (√13/3)2 + 8 × (3/2)2

⇒ (52 × 9/13 – 9 × 4/9)/(18 × 13/9 + 8 × 9/4)

⇒ (36 – 4)/(26 + 18)

⇒ 32/44

⇒ 8/11

∴ The required value is 8/11

questions.question: \(\frac{{1 - \tan A}}{{1 + \tan A}} = \frac{{\tan 3^\circ \tan 15^\circ \tan 30^\circ \tan 75^\circ \tan 87^\circ }}{{\tan 27^\circ \tan 39^\circ \tan 51^\circ \tan 60^\circ \tan 63^\circ }}\) , then the value of cot A is:

GIven:

\(\frac{{1 - \tan A}}{{1 + \tan A}} = \frac{{\tan 3^\circ \tan 15^\circ \tan 30^\circ \tan 75^\circ \tan 87^\circ }}{{\tan 27^\circ \tan 39^\circ \tan 51^\circ \tan 60^\circ \tan 63^\circ }}\)

Formula used:

If  A + B = 90° 

Then tan A × tan B = 1

Tanθ = 1/cotθ 

Tan 30° = 1/√3

Tan 60° = √3

Calculation:

Using the above formula 

⇒ tan 3° × tan 87° = 1

⇒ tan 15° × tan 75° = 1 

⇒ tan 27° × tan 63° = 1

⇒ tan 39° × tan 51° = 1

Put values in the given equation we get

⇒ (1 - tan A)/(1 + tan A) = (1/√3)/√3

⇒ (1 - tan A)/(1 + tan A) = 1/3

⇒ 3 - 3tan A = 1 + tan A

⇒ 4 tan A = 2

⇒ tan A = 2/4

⇒ cot A = 2

∴ The value of cot A is 2.

 sin (π − θ) + sin (\(\frac{π}{2}\) - θ)

questions.question: If cosec A + cot A = 3, 0 ≤ A ≤ 90°, then find the value of cos A.
questions.questionHtml: If cosec A + cot A = 3, 0 ≤ A ≤ 90°, then find the value of cos A.
questions.solution:
Cot A + Cosec A = 3 ⇒ (Cos A /Sin A) + (1/Sin A) = 3 ⇒ Cos A + 1 = 3SinA

⇒ (Cos A + 1)2 = 9Sin2A ⇒ Cos2A + 2CosA + 1 = 9 (1 – Cos2A) ⇒ 10Cos2A + 2Cos A – 8 = 0

⇒ 5Cos2A + Cos A – 4 = 0 ⇒ (5CosA – 4) (Cos A + 1) = 0 ⇒ 5CosA – 4 = 0 or Cos A + 1 = 0 

⇒ CosA = 4/5 or CosA = -1 ⇒ cos A = 4/5( Since, ∠A is an acute angle)

questions.question: If 14 sin 2 θ + 3 sin θ - 5 = 0, 0° < θ < 90°, then the value of \(\frac{\sec 2\theta + \cot 2\theta}{\rm cosec 2\theta + \tan 2\theta }\) is:
questions.questionHtml: If 14 sin2 θ + 3 sin θ - 5 = 0, 0° < θ < 90°, then the value of \(\frac{\sec 2\theta + \cot 2\theta}{\rm cosec 2\theta + \tan 2\theta }\) is:
questions.solution:
14 sin2 θ + 3 sin θ - 5 = 0

⇒ 14 sin2 θ + 10 sin θ - 7 sin θ - 5 = 0 ⇒ 2 sin θ(7sin θ + 5) -1(7sin θ + 5) = 0 ⇒ (7sin θ + 5)(2sin θ -  1) = 0

7sin θ + 5 = 0 ⇒ sin θ = -5/7 [ this value rejected, as  0° < θ < 90° ]

Now, 2sin θ - 1 = 0 ⇒ sin θ = 1/2 ⇒ θ = 30° 

\(\frac{\sec 2\theta + \cot 2\theta}{\rm cosec 2\theta + \tan 2\theta }\) ⇒ \(\frac{\sec 2\times 30 + \cot 2\times 30}{\rm cosec 2\times 30 + \tan 2\times 30 }\) ⇒ \(\frac{\sec 60 + \cot 60}{\rm cosec 60 + \tan 60 }\) ⇒ \(\frac{2 + \frac{1}{\sqrt3}}{\rm \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} + \sqrt{3} }\) ⇒ \(\frac{1 + 2\sqrt3}{5}\)

questions.question: If \(\frac{5 \cot \theta + \sqrt 3 \:cosec\: \theta}{2\sqrt3\: cosec\: \theta + 3 \cot \theta}=1,0^{\circ} <\theta<90^{\circ}\) , then the value of \(\frac{\frac{7}{2} \cot^2 \theta- \frac{3}{4} \:cosec^2 \theta}{4 \sin^2 \theta+\frac{3}{2} \tan^2 \theta}\) will be:
questions.questionHtml: If \(\frac{5 \cot \theta + \sqrt 3 \:cosec\: \theta}{2\sqrt3\: cosec\: \theta + 3 \cot \theta}=1,0^{\circ} <\theta<90^{\circ}\), then the value of \(\frac{\frac{7}{2} \cot^2 \theta- \frac{3}{4} \:cosec^2 \theta}{4 \sin^2 \theta+\frac{3}{2} \tan^2 \theta}\) will be:
questions.solution:
Given:

\(\frac{5 \cot θ + √ 3 \:cosec\: θ}{2√3\: cosec\: θ + 3 \cot θ}=1,0^{\circ} <θ<90^{\circ}\)

Formula used:

cotθ = cosθ/sinθ 

cosecθ = 1/sinθ 

Calculation:

\(\frac{5 \cot θ + √ 3 \:cosec\: θ}{2√3\: cosec\: θ + 3 \cot θ}=1,0^{\circ} <θ<90^{\circ}\)

⇒ 5cotθ + √3cosecθ = 2√3cosecθ + 3cotθ 

⇒ (5cotθ – 3cotθ) = (2√3cosecθ – √3cosecθ)

⇒ 2cotθ = √3cosecθ 

⇒ 2 × cosθ/sinθ = √3 × 1/sinθ 

⇒ 2cosθ = √3

⇒ cosθ = √3/2 = cos 30° 

So, θ = 30° 

Now,

The value of \(\frac{\frac{7}{2} \cot^2 θ- \frac{3}{4} \:cosec^2 θ}{4 \sin^2 θ+\frac{3}{2} \tan^2 θ}\)

⇒ (7/2 cot230° – 3/4 cosec230°)/(4 sin230° + 3/2 tan230°)

⇒ 7/2 × (√3)2 – 3/4 × (2)2/4 × (1/2)2 + 3/2 × (1/√3)2

⇒ (7/2 × 3) – (3/4 × 4)/(4 × 1/4) + (3/2 × 1/3)

⇒ (21/2 – 3)/(1 + 1/2)

⇒ (21 – 6)/2/(2 + 1)/2

⇒ (15/2)/(3/2)

⇒ (15/2 × 2/3)

⇒ 5

∴ The required value is 5

questions.question: If 3 sin 2 θ + 4cos θ - 4 = 0, 0° < θ < 90 ° , then the value of (cosec 2 θ + cot 2 θ) is
questions.questionHtml: If 3 sin2 θ + 4cos θ - 4 = 0, 0° < θ  < 90°, then the value of (cosec2 θ + cot2 θ) is
questions.solution:
3sin2θ + 4cosθ - 4 = 0

⇒ 3(1 - cos2θ) + 4cosθ - 4 = 0 ⇒ - 3cos2θ + 4cosθ - 1 = 0 ⇒ 3cos2θ - 4cosθ + 1 = 0 ⇒ 3cos2θ - 3cosθ - cosθ  + 1 = 0 ⇒ 3cosθ(cosθ - 1) - 1(cosθ  - 1) = 0 ⇒ (cosθ - 1)(3cosθ - 1) = 0

So, cosθ = 1, 1/3, but cosθ = 1 is not possible because it is given 0° < θ  < 90° and cos0° = 1 so, cosθ = 1/3 = B/H

H2 = B2 + P2 ⇒ 32 = 12 + P2 ⇒ P = 2√2 

So, cosec2θ + cot2θ ⇒ (3/2√2)2 + (1/2√2)2 ⇒ (9/8) + (1/8) ⇒ (9 + 1)/8 ⇒ 10/8 = 5/4

questions.question: The value of \(\frac{3cos^227^\circ-5 + 3cos^263^\circ }{tan^232^\circ + 4 - cosec^2 58^\circ}\) + sin35°cos55° + cos35°sin55° is:
questions.questionHtml: The value of \(\frac{3cos^227^\circ-5 + 3cos^263^\circ }{tan^232^\circ + 4 - cosec^2 58^\circ}\) + sin35°cos55° + cos35°sin55° is:
questions.solution:
Given:

\(\frac{3cos^227^\circ-5 + 3cos^263^\circ }{tan^232^\circ + 4 - cosec^2 58^\circ}\)

Formula used:

sin2θ + cos2θ = 1

tan2θ = sec2θ - 1 'or' sec2θ - tan2θ = 1

Calculation:

According to the question

\(\frac{3cos^227^\circ-5 + 3cos^263^\circ }{tan^232^\circ + 4 - cosec^2 58^\circ}\) + sin35° cos55° + cos35° sin55°

⇒ (3cos227° – 5 + 3sin227°)/(tan232° + 4 – sec232°) + sin35°sin35° + cos35°cos35° 

⇒ 3(sin227°  + cos227°) – 5/4 –  (sec232° - tan232 ) + (sin235° + cos235°)

⇒ [3(1) – 5]/(4 – 1) + 1

⇒ (3 – 5)3 + 1

⇒ -2/3 + 1

⇒ (-2 + 3)/3

⇒ 1/3

∴ The required value is \(\frac{1}{3}\)

questions.question: If cosθ = √ 3/2 , then the value of \(\frac{2 - \sin^2 θ}{1 - \cot^2 θ}\) + (sec 2 θ + cosec θ) is
questions.questionHtml: If cosθ = √ 3/2, then the value of \(\frac{2 - \sin^2 θ}{1 - \cot^2 θ}\) + (sec2 θ + cosec θ) is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Since cos θ = √3/2, the standard value for θ is 30°.

Substitute θ = 30° directly into the expression:

Value = (2 − sin2 30°) / (1 − cot2 30°) + (sec2 30° + cosec 30°)

Value = (2 − 1/4) / (1 − 3) + (4/3 + 2) = (7/4)/(−2) + 10/3 = −7/8 + 10/3

Value = (−21 + 80) / 24 = 59/24.

∴ The correct answer is 59/24.

Alternate Method

Given: cos θ = √3/2

Formula Used:

1. sin2 θ + cos2 θ = 1

2. cot θ = cos θ / sin θ

3. sec θ = 1 / cos θ

4. cosec θ = 1 / sin θ

Step-by-step Calculations:

⇒ If cos θ = √3/2, then sin θ = √(1 − (3/4)) = √(1/4) = 1/2.

⇒ cot θ = (√3/2) / (1/2) = √3.

⇒ sec θ = 1 / (√3/2) = 2/√3.

⇒ cosec θ = 1 / (1/2) = 2.

⇒ Expression Part 1 = (2 − sin2 θ) / (1 − cot2 θ) = (2 − (1/2)2) / (1 − (√3)2)

⇒ Part 1 = (2 − 1/4) / (1 − 3) = (7/4) / (−2) = −7/8.

⇒ Expression Part 2 = (sec2 θ + cosec θ) = (2/√3)2 + 2 = 4/3 + 2 = 10/3.

⇒ Total Value = −7/8 + 10/3 = (−21 + 80) / 24 = 59/24.

∴ The correct answer is 59/24.

Additional Information

Standard Trigonometric Values for 30°

For 30°: sin = 1/2, cos = √3/2, tan = 1/√3, cot = √3, sec = 2/√3, cosec = 2.

Pythagorean Identities

sin2 θ + cos2 θ = 1 | 1 + tan2 θ = sec2 θ | 1 + cot2 θ = cosec2 θ.

Reciprocal Relations

cosec θ = 1/sin θ, sec θ = 1/cos θ, cot θ = 1/tan θ.

questions.question: The value of \(\frac{\tan 50^\circ + \sec 50^\circ}{\cot 40^\circ + \text{cosec} \ 40^\circ}\) + cos 2 65° + sin 65° cos 25° + tan 30° is
questions.questionHtml: The value of \(\frac{\tan 50^\circ + \sec 50^\circ}{\cot 40^\circ + \text{cosec} \ 40^\circ}\) + cos2 65° + sin 65° cos 25° + tan 30° is
questions.solution:
Given: 

 \(\frac{\tan 50^\circ + \sec 50^\circ}{\cot 40^\circ + \text{cosec} \ 40^\circ}\) + cos2 65° + sin 65° cos 25° + tan 30°

Concept used:

Cot (90° - θ) = Tan θ 

Cosec (90° - θ) = Sec θ 

Sin (90° - θ) =  Cos θ 

Sin2 θ + Cos2 θ  = 1

Calculation:

\(\frac{\tan 50^\circ + \sec 50^\circ}{\cot 40^\circ + \text{cosec} \ 40^\circ}\) + cos2 65° + sin 65° cos 25° + tan 30°

⇒ {Cot (90 - 50)° + Cosec (90 - 50)°}/(Cot 40° + Cosec 40°) + cos2 65° + sin 65° sin (90 - 25)° + tan 30°

⇒ (Cot 40° + Cosec 40°)/(Cot 40° + Cosec 40°) + (cos2 65° + sin2 65°) + (1/√3)

⇒ 1 + 1 + (1/√3)

⇒ 2 + √3/3

⇒ (6 + √ 3)/3

∴ The value of \(\frac{\tan 50^\circ + \sec 50^\circ}{\cot 40^\circ + \text{cosec} \ 40^\circ}\)  cos2 65° + sin 65° cos 25° + tan 30° is  (6 + √ 3)/3.

questions.question: Find x if sin x = \( - \frac{1}{2}\) .
questions.questionHtml: Find x if sin x = \( - \frac{1}{2}\).
questions.solution:
Given

Sin x = - 1/2

Concept used

If Sin x is negative then sin lies in 3rd quadrant or 4th quadrant, according to the following details:

Calculation

Sin x = - sin (1/2)

⇒ Sin x = - sin (π/6)

⇒ Sin x = sin (2π - π/6)

⇒ Sin x = sin (12π - π)/6

⇒ Sin x = sin (11π/6)

∴ x is 11π/6

Important Points

It is important for a candidate to remember the basic relation of conversion from degree to radian:

180° = π radians

questions.question: If \(sin\theta = \frac{2\sqrt{ab}}{a+b}\) , a > b > 0, then the value of \(\frac{cos\theta + 1}{cos \theta - 1}\) will be:
questions.questionHtml: If \(sin\theta = \frac{2\sqrt{ab}}{a+b}\), a > b > 0, then the value of \(\frac{cos\theta + 1}{cos \theta - 1}\) will be:
questions.solution:
Given:

\(sinθ = \frac{2√{ab}}{a+b}\)

Formula used:

b2 = h2 –  p2

Calculation:

Sinθ = p/h = 2√ab/a + b

b2 = h2 – p2

⇒ b2 = (a + b)2 – (2√ab)2

⇒ b2 = (a + b)2 – 4ab 

⇒ b2 = (a – b)2

⇒ b = (a – b)

Now,

cosθ = b/h = (a – b)/(a + b)

\(\frac{cos\theta + 1}{cos \theta - 1}\) = [(a – b)/(a + b) + 1]/[(a – b)(/(a + b) – 1]

⇒ (a – b + a + b)/(a – b – a – b)

⇒ 2a/(-2b)

⇒ -a/b

∴ The required value is -a/b

questions.question: If \(\frac{{\sec θ + \tan θ }}{{\sec θ - \tan θ }} = \frac{5}{3}\) , 0° < θ < 90°, then what is the value of (cosec θ + cos θ + cot θ)?
questions.questionHtml: If \(\frac{{\sec θ + \tan θ }}{{\sec θ - \tan θ }} = \frac{5}{3}\), 0° < θ < 90°, then what is the value of (cosec θ + cos θ + cot θ)?
questions.solution:
Given:

\(\frac{{\sec θ + \tan θ }}{{\sec θ - \tan θ }} = \frac{5}{3}\)

Concept used:

If

\(\frac{{a+ b }}{{a - b }} = \frac{c}{d}\), then \(\frac{{a}}{{b }} = \frac{c+d}{c-d}\)

Calculation:

\(\frac{{\sec θ + \tan θ }}{{\sec θ - \tan θ }} = \frac{5}{3}\)

⇒ \(\frac{{\sec θ }}{{\\tan θ }} = \frac{5+3}{5-3}\)

⇒ \(\frac{{\sec θ }}{{\\tan θ }} = \frac{4}{1}\)

⇒ cosec θ  =  4

We have, cos θ = √15/4, cot θ = √15

The value of cosec θ + cos θ + cot θ

⇒ 4 + √15/4 + √15

⇒ \(\frac{{16 + 5\sqrt {15} }}{4}\)

∴ The value of (cosec θ + cos θ + cot θ) is \(\frac{{16 + 5\sqrt {15} }}{4}\).

questions.questionHtml: If sin θ + tan θ = p and tan θ - sin θ = q, then which of the relation satisfies for given values of p and q?
questions.solution:
Squaring and subtracting eq 2 from eq 1.

⇒ p2 - q2 = sin2 θ + tan2 θ + 2sin θ tan θ - (sin2 θ + tan2 θ - 2sin θ tan θ) ⇒ p2 - q2 = 4sin θ tan θ

4sin θ tan θ = 4√( sin2 θ tan2 θ) = 4√( sin2 θ (sec2 θ - 1) = 4√( sin2 θ/ cos2 θ - sin2 θ) = 4√( tan2 θ - sin2 θ) = 4√pq

p2 - q2 = 4√pq

questions.question: If sin α + cos α = \(\frac{2}{\sqrt3}\) , then what is (tan α + cot α) equal to?
questions.questionHtml: If sin α + cos α = \(\frac{2}{\sqrt3}\), then what is (tan α + cot α) equal to?
questions.solution:
sin α + cos α = \(\frac{2}{√3}\)

⇒ sin2 α + cos2 α + 2sin α.cos α = (2/√3)2 ⇒  1 + 2sin α.cos α = 4/3 ⇒ 2sin α.cos α = 4/3 - 1 = 1/3 ⇒ sin α.cos α = 1/6

tan α + cot α = (sin α/cos α) + (cos α/sin α)  = (sin2 α + cos2 α )/(sin α.cos α) = 1/(sin α.cos α) = 6

questions.question: If 4sin 2 θ = 3(1+ cos θ), 0° < θ < 90°, then what is the value of (2tan θ + 4sin θ - sec θ)?
questions.questionHtml: If 4sin2 θ = 3(1+ cos θ), 0° < θ < 90°, then what is the value of (2tan θ + 4sin θ - sec θ)?
questions.solution:
Given:

4sin2 θ = 3(1+ cos θ), 0° < θ < 90°

Calculation:

4 (1 - cos2 θ) = 3 + 3cos θ

⇒ 4 - 4cos2 θ = 3 + 3cos θ

⇒ 4cos2 θ + 3cos θ - 1 = 0

⇒ 4cos2 θ + 4cos θ - cos θ - 1 = 0

⇒ 4cos θ (cos θ + 1) - 1 (cos θ + 1) = 0

⇒ (4cos θ - 1) (cos θ + 1) = 0

⇒ cos θ + 1 = 0 ⇒ cos θ = - 1 [Not possible because 0° < θ < 90]

⇒ 4cos θ - 1 = 0 ⇒ cos θ = 1/4

We can get all value by using the image below,

The height will be = √(42 - 12) = √(16 - 1) = √15

So, (2tan θ + 4sin θ - sec θ) = (2 × √15) + (4 × √15/4) - 4

= 2√15 + √15 - 4

= 3√15 - 4

∴ The value of (2tan θ + 4sin θ - sec θ) is 3√15 - 4

So,

questions.question: \(\frac{(1+\cos \theta)(cosec \theta-\cot \theta)\sec \theta}{\sin \theta(1-\sin\theta)(\sec \theta+\tan \theta)}=?\)
questions.questionHtml: \(\frac{(1+\cos \theta)(cosec \theta-\cot \theta)\sec \theta}{\sin \theta(1-\sin\theta)(\sec \theta+\tan \theta)}=?\)
questions.solution:
Given:

\(\frac{(1+\cos θ)(cosec θ-\cot θ)\sec θ}{\sin θ(1-\sinθ)(\sec θ+\tan θ)}=?\)

Formula used:

cosecθ = 1/sinθ 

secθ = 1/cosθ 

cotθ = cosθ/sinθ

tanθ = sinθ/cosθ 

1 – cos2θ = sin2θ 

1 – sin2θ = cos2θ 

Calculation:

\(\frac{(1+\cos θ)(cosec θ-\cot θ)\sec θ}{\sin θ(1-\sinθ)(\sec θ+\tan θ)}=?\)

⇒ [(1 + cosθ)(1/sinθ – cosθ/sinθ) 1/cosθ]/[sinθ(1 – sinθ)(1/cosθ + sinθ/cosθ)]

⇒ [(1 + cosθ)(1 – cosθ/sinθ) 1/cosθ]/[sinθ(1 – sinθ)(1 + sinθ/cosθ)]

⇒ [(1 – cos2θ)/sinθ × 1/cosθ]/[sinθ (1 – sin2θ)/cosθ]

⇒ (sin2θ/sinθ × 1/cosθ)/(sinθ × cos2θ/cosθ)

⇒ (sinθ/cosθ)/(sinθ × cosθ)

⇒ 1/cos2θ 

⇒ sec2θ 

∴ The value of ? is sec2θ

questions.question: If \(({\cos ^2}θ - 1)(2{\sec ^2}θ ) + {\sec ^2}θ + 2{\tan ^2}θ = 2\) , 0º < θ < 90º, then \(\frac{{\left( {\cos ec\theta + \cos \theta } \right)}}{{\left( {\cos ec\theta - \cos \theta } \right)}}\) is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: If \(({\cos ^2}θ - 1)(2{\sec ^2}θ ) + {\sec ^2}θ + 2{\tan ^2}θ = 2\), 0º < θ < 90º, then \(\frac{{\left( {\cos ec\theta + \cos \theta } \right)}}{{\left( {\cos ec\theta - \cos \theta } \right)}}\) is equal to:
questions.solution:
Formula Used:

Sin2θ + Cos2θ = 1, Sec2θ = Tan2θ + 1

Calculation:

If (cos2θ – 1)(2sec2θ) + sec2θ + 2tan2θ = 2, 0° < θ < 90°

⇒ – (1 – cos2θ)(2sec2θ) + sec2θ + 2tan2θ = 2

⇒ – (sin2θ)(2sec2θ) + tan2θ + 1 + 2tan2θ = 2 (By using above formulas)

⇒ – 2(sin2θ)/(cos2θ) + 3tan2θ = 2 – 1

⇒ – 2tan2θ + 3tan2θ = 1 or tan2θ = 1

⇒ tanθ = 1, θ = 45°

Now, as given in the question

⇒ (cosecθ + cosθ)/(cosecθ – cosθ) = (cosec45° + cos45°)/(cosec45° - cos45°)

⇒   (√2 + 1/√2)(√2 – 1/√2) = (2 + 1)/(2 – 1) = 3

questions.question: In ΔPQR, ∠PQR = 135°, PQ = 8√2 cm and PR = 17 cm. What is the length (in cm) of QR?
questions.questionHtml: In ΔPQR, ∠PQR = 135°, PQ = 8√2 cm and PR = 17 cm. What is the length (in cm) of QR?
questions.solution:
Given:

∠PQR = 135° 

PQ = 8√2 cm

PR = 17 cm

Formula used:

Cosine rule - cosθ = (b2 + c2 – a2)/2bc

Calculation:

Let the value of b be x

According to the question

Cos 135° = [x2 + (8√2)2 – (17)2]/2 × x × 8√2

⇒ -1/√2 = (x2 + 128 – 289)/(2 × x × 8√2)

⇒ -1/√2 = (x2 – 161)/2 × x × 8√2

⇒ -16x = x2 – 161

⇒ x2 + 16x – 161 = 0

⇒ x2 + 23x – 7x – 161 = 0

⇒ x(x + 23) – 7(x + 23) = 0

⇒ (x + 23) (x – 7) = 0

⇒ x = -23, 7

∴ The required value of QR is 7
